note: VARIETY: Colloquial spoken QUÉBÉCOIS (Quebec French), not standard France French. This is the whole point — the previous build was standard French (98.7% identical to fra_for_eng) because it anchored to standard-French golden seeds. REGISTER: everyday spoken Quebec. KEY DISTINCTIVE FORMS to use consistently: chu (je suis), m'as (je vais / going-to future), the -tu question particle (Tu viens-tu? Y'é-tu correc?), y'/a (il/elle in speech), pas de… / pantoute (not at all), tsé (you know), faque (so/therefore), ben (well/very), asteure or là-là (now), correc (fine/ok), c'est le fun / écœurant (it's great), en masse (a lot/plenty), pogner (to catch/grab), jaser (to chat). LEXIS: char (car, not voiture), blonde (girlfriend), chum (boyfriend/buddy), magasiner (to shop), dépanneur (corner store), fin de semaine (weekend, not week-end), frette (cold), niaiser (to joke/mess around), tantôt (in a bit / earlier), bienvenue (you're welcome). Keep tu/toi informal throughout. ⚠️ These are native-quality Québécois anchors — match this register; do NOT drift to France French (pas de 'nous', use 'on'; pas de over-formal 'vous').
